archetype.name: Game Manager (check-down backup)
archetype.definition: A tall, pocket-bound backup who keeps the ball underneath and out of harm's way, takes few risks, and has yet to show he can push the ball downfield to drive an offense.

report.headline: Safe and accurate underneath, but nothing downfield and nothing around him
report.take:
Tanner McKee is now listed as the Eagles' QB1 after two straight appearances: a Week 6 start against Carolina, then most of Week 7 against Dallas in a game Jalen Hurts started. The dossier doesn't say why Hurts is out of the picture, so the useful question is what McKee is as a starter. So far the answer is a cautious distributor. His intended air yards sit at 6.89, he throws 2.92 yards short of the sticks on average, and only 17.5% of his throws go into tight windows. That keeps him clean: one interception, an intPct of 1.3 (13th of 45), and no fumbles. It also keeps the offense small. His -0.141 EPA per dropback ranks 39th of 45, and his 5.33 yards per attempt ranks 43rd.

The split by depth tells the story. On throws under 10 air yards he completes 71.2% with a CPOE of exactly 0. That's competent, ordinary work, slightly positive in EPA. Past that line everything breaks. Throws of 10+ yards run at 33.3% completion and -0.306 EPA. The deep shots have been the damage: he hasn't completed any of his six attempts of 20+ yards, and those six throws alone cost -8.7 EPA, most of his whole-season deficit. Oddly, his charted bad-throw rate is only 10% (4th of 38), a big improvement from the 23.3% of his 2025 spot start. The misses are coming more from timing and decisions than from the ball sailing.

Context matters, and it's ugly. The offense ranks 29th in EPA, Lane Johnson is out for the year, center Jake Majors sat as a coach's decision, and DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks were both inactive in Week 7. He's been throwing to Dallas Goedert, rookie Makai Lemon and Darius Cooper behind a patched line, with Saquon Barkley hobbled. Lemon has been the bright spot at 0.265 EPA per target. Pressure hasn't been the problem, though: he's been pressured on just 14.5% of dropbacks, 4th lowest. So the struggles are mostly his and the receivers', not the line's.

The score splits sharpen it. Within one score he's been poor at -0.197 EPA with a -12.4 CPOE. Trailing by nine or more, against softer coverage, he has completed 71.9% with a +7 CPOE. His 2024 one-game cameo (0.31 EPA per play, 2nd that week's list) shows a higher ceiling exists. Two-plus seasons of tiny samples, though, say he lands somewhere around a below-average starter who won't lose you the game with turnovers but rarely wins it through the air.

strengths.title: Ball security and low turnover risk
strengths.body: He has one interception and no fumbles across 86 dropbacks. That comes straight from his conservative read structure, with short targets and few tight windows. It should hold as long as he keeps playing this way, and it gives a bad team a floor.

strengths.title: Clean, on-schedule short game
strengths.body: Under 10 air yards he's completing 71.2% at expected rates with slightly positive EPA, and his charted bad-throw rate is among the lowest in the league. That's a real change from the scattershot 2025 start. The 2025 sample was one game, so treat the improvement as encouraging rather than settled.

strengths.title: Finishing in the red zone
strengths.body: He has two touchdowns on four red-zone attempts. A big pocket passer can see and throw over the condensed field. It's a four-throw sample, so expect his touchdown rate to stay below league average rather than climb off this.

concerns.title: No functioning downfield game
concerns.body: His six deep attempts have produced no completions and -8.7 EPA, and throws of 10+ yards overall sit at a -17 CPOE. Part of this is the missing receivers: Smith and Wicks were out, and Lemon is a rookie. Six throws is a small sample. Still, the intermediate completion rate is also weak, so defenses can sit on the short stuff until he proves otherwise.

concerns.title: Struggles when the game is close
concerns.body: Within one score his EPA per play is -0.197 with a -12.4 CPOE, far worse than when trailing big. That's the opposite of what a starter needs. The garbage-time line flatters his totals, and the competitive-state line is closer to his true level until a healthier receiver group changes it.

concerns.title: Depleted line and receiver room
concerns.body: Lane Johnson is out for the season and Majors was benched for Week 7. That puts a thin offense, 29th in EPA, in front of a backup. Pressure has been light so far, but his sacks still run at 2.5 a game. Those sacks are the bill for holding the ball when nothing is open underneath.

trend.note: His efficiency improved from -8.6 EPA against Carolina to -3.4 against a bottom-three Dallas defense. He got there by shrinking the game: aggressiveness fell from 22.2% to 11.4% and intended air yards from 8.1 to 5.3. That's a safer version of the same limited player, not a breakout.

nextGame.headline: Leaky Washington pass defense and a weak rush suit him
nextGame.body:
Washington is a soft pass defense: 26th in pass EPA, 25th in sack rate, 24th in hit rate. It's also the league's strongest pass funnel, with opponents passing 7.2 points more than normal against it. That points to volume and a clean pocket for McKee. The catch is that Washington is good on short throws (7th in short EPA), which is exactly where McKee lives. Its deep EPA allowed is generous, at 22nd. If he's going to finally hit something over the top, this is the spot. The clearest edge is at tight end: Washington has let TE1s score 9.1 PPR points over their averages, worst in the league, which sets up Goedert as his steady outlet.

Availability swings this. Smith and Wicks carry estimated returns of game day; getting either back gives McKee a real intermediate option, while their absence leaves him leaning on Goedert and Lemon again. Majors' return at center and Barkley's back/hamstring are worth watching too. On Washington's side, DT Javon Kinlaw and DE Charles Omenihu are questionable, which could thin an already modest rush further. Terry McLaurin is out for the year and Mariota is questionable, which may cap Washington's scoring and keep this a low-total (40.5) one-score game. That's the state where McKee has been worst. Early forecasts show gusts in the mid-20s at an outdoor stadium; worth checking later in the week, but not something to build on yet.

keyMatchups.title: Goedert against a soft spot
keyMatchups.body: Goedert leads McKee's targets, though at only breakeven EPA. Washington has been the worst defense in the league against lead tight ends, both in fantasy points over average and EPA allowed. Expect a steady flow of middle-of-the-field throws, where McKee has been most efficient on a small sample.

keyMatchups.title: Short throws into a stingy underneath
keyMatchups.body: Washington's short-area defense ranks 7th, while its deep EPA allowed is among the worst. McKee's whole game is short. Unless he converts some intermediate and deep throws, his checkdowns run straight into what this defense does well.

keyMatchups.title: Weak pass rush versus patched line
keyMatchups.body: Washington ranks 25th in sack rate and 24th in hit rate, with two front-seven players questionable. That's a break for a line missing Johnson. It should keep his sack total manageable and let him stay in rhythm.

nextGame.watch: Whether he completes even one or two throws beyond 15 yards. Washington's deep defense is the softest part of its game, and that would tell us whether the Week 7 shrinking was a choice or a ceiling.

restOfSeason.body:
As long as he's QB1, expect volume to carry his box scores more than efficiency. The Eagles' defense ranks 27th and can't rush the passer, so he'll be throwing from behind often. That inflates attempts and yards and lets him pile up his best work in trailing scripts. Per-game passing yards around 195 to 245 are realistic, with roughly a touchdown a game. The interception rate should drift up toward normal from its current low; one pick in 80 throws is partly luck. The deep-ball zero will improve somewhat by regression alone, and more if Smith and Wicks return. His efficiency is likely to settle in the -0.15 to -0.02 EPA per dropback range: below average, but not a disaster.

The things that hold up are his short-area accuracy, low sack exposure behind light pressure, and a conservative style that limits giveaways. What won't hold up is the red-zone touchdown efficiency on four throws. His starting role itself is the biggest unknown, since the dossier doesn't explain Hurts' status, and a change there ends the outlook entirely.
swingFactors: Jalen Hurts' status and how long McKee holds QB1
DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks returning
Any completed deep shots changing how defenses play him

confidence.note: Two games and 86 dropbacks, a depleted supporting cast, and an unexplained QB situation; career samples are one game a year.
